sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name any two types of photojournalism.
questions.answer: Sports photojournalism and war photojournalism (also glamour, spot news, travel, wildlife).

questions.q: Mention any two advantages of a good composition.
questions.answer: It gives the picture impact and contrast, makes it appealing and balanced, and lets the viewer understand its meaning at once.

questions.q: Who is a photojournalist? What is meant by wildlife photojournalism?
questions.answer: A photojournalist is a news photographer whose pictures support news stories; wildlife photojournalism photographs animals, needing advanced equipment and knowledge of animal behaviour and terrain.

questions.q: Briefly discuss the process of bringing out a photo feature in a newspaper or magazine.
questions.answer: The editor conceives it and briefs the photo editor, who chooses the photographer and topic and perhaps a reporter, and selects the best pictures that tell the whole story.

questions.q: What is spot news photojournalism?
questions.answer: Covering events that make day-to-day news such as political events, crime and accidents; the most common and demanding type.

questions.q: What is the rule of thirds?
questions.answer: A framing rule that elements should fall near the intersections of lines dividing the frame into three rows and three columns.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Photojournalism): attempt B or Module A. Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the role of photographs in news reporting.
questions.answer: Photographs support written news with authority and emphasis, convey the news at a glance (a single picture is worth a thousand words), enhance the lead story, tell stories through photo essays and use composition for impact.

questions.q: Briefly discuss the points of consideration of the photo editor for selecting a picture in a newspaper.
questions.answer: The major news events of the day (a picture that enhances the lead story), the hard-hitting nature of the picture that tells a story, and reader interest such as local events.

questions.q: What is photojournalism? Explain the types with examples.
questions.answer: Photojournalism is news photography supporting stories: sports, war, glamour, spot news, travel and wildlife photojournalism, by employed or freelance photojournalists and now web-based.
